title: Cities: Skylines | Franklin, Episode 10: Law & Order
premise: Donoteat01 builds a model of Eastern State Penitentiary and uses it to argue that isolation, surveillance and compulsory labor link nineteenth-century prison reform to coercive incarceration today. The historical and political claims are his.
coverage: Prison modeling and city construction accompany a history of punishment and an architectural slide lecture. Historical and political claims are the presenter’s. Brief inserts may be missed, and sound-cue placement is approximate.

panels.heading: Series emblem
panels.description: Orange Franklin lettering and Liberty Bell emblem on black.
panels.camera: Static title graphic.
panels.action: No character action.

panels.heading: Introduce the prison
panels.description: Aerial view of the modeled prison carries a DONOTEAT series overlay.
panels.camera: The opening cuts from the logo to the aerial model, then reframes the complex from several angles.
panels.action: Title overlay; prison remains stationary.

panels.heading: 1836: Law & Order
panels.description: Episode title overlays the Blender prison model.
panels.camera: Cut to desktop capture; fixed interface with viewport reframing.
panels.action: Presenter begins the episode while the model is edited.
panels.visualGag: Saying “law and order” sets off the DUN-DUN sting from the television series over the modeling footage. The next panel repeats the gag straight away and comments on it.

sound.text: Law & Order’s DUN-DUN sting answers the phrase “law and order.”

panels.heading: Law & Order repeats: every time
panels.description: Prison modeling continues as “law and order” and the television sting recur.
panels.camera: Desktop capture of the model and its reference images, reframed from moment to moment; the presenter never appears on screen.
panels.action: Work on the asset and its reference images continues under the narrator’s reaction.

sound.text: Law & Order’s DUN-DUN sting plays again.

panels.visualGag: The phrase “law and order” comes up again and the sting fires again. The narrator reacts with “is it going to do this every time,” which turns the sting into a running joke.
panels.notes: After this reaction, each later DUN-DUN plays as a callback.

panels.heading: The game’s simple crime loop
panels.description: Roads, rowhouses and a small police-looking vehicle illustrate the game system.
panels.camera: Game views reframe as the car drives along the streets.
panels.action: Vehicle travels through the modeled neighborhood; narration questions deterrence.
panels.visualGag: “Law and order” comes back while the narrator critiques the game, bringing the DUN-DUN sting and the every-time joke with it. The gameplay simply illustrates the point.

sound.text: Law & Order’s DUN-DUN sting returns.

panels.heading: Architecture, not policing yet
panels.description: Blender workspace shows the developing stone prison facade.
panels.camera: Desktop capture with the model viewport reframed between cuts.
panels.action: Mesh construction continues beneath the explanation of the time-lapse premise.
panels.visualGag: Heading toward the familiar trigger, the narrator swerves: “law and … uh, imprisonment.” Dodging the phrase calls back the DUN-DUN and every-time joke while the prison modeling carries on.

sound.text: “Law and … uh, imprisonment”: the hesitation sidesteps the Law & Order trigger and calls back the DUN-DUN and every-time joke.

panels.heading: Sargon mistaken-identity setup
panels.description: Blender model precedes a three-image Sargon joke: Paul Joseph Watson against a map, YouTuber Sargon of Akkad (Carl Benjamin) at a podcast microphone, then an ancient bronze head representing the historical Sargon.
panels.camera: Desktop capture of the model viewport, just before the first face insert.
panels.action: Modeling continues beneath narration.
panels.visualGag: Saying “Sargon of Akkad” first brings up two wrong modern men: Paul Joseph Watson, then Carl Benjamin, the YouTuber who calls himself Sargon of Akkad. Both are waved off before an ancient bronze head reveals the historical Sargon.

panels.heading: First wrong Sargon: Paul Joseph Watson
panels.description: Paul Joseph Watson in a light-blue shirt against a world map overlays the prison model.
panels.camera: Cut to a static photograph over the model.
panels.action: Frozen front-facing modern man; no acted historical scene.
panels.visualGag: The ancient ruler’s name brings up Paul Joseph Watson instead, and the narrator says “No, not that guy.” Carl Benjamin, the YouTuber called Sargon of Akkad, comes next, and only then the historical Sargon.

panels.heading: Second wrong Sargon: YouTuber Sargon of Akkad (Carl Benjamin)
panels.description: Carl Benjamin, the anti-feminist YouTuber Sargon of Akkad and UKIP election candidate, appears bearded and wearing headphones at a podcast microphone against red curtains.
panels.camera: Static photograph insert over moving modeling capture.
panels.action: Man is frozen beside a microphone; no acted scene.
panels.visualGag: “No, not that guy either” dismisses Carl Benjamin, the modern YouTuber who goes by Sargon of Akkad. He is the second wrong answer after Paul Joseph Watson; the ancient head that follows is the real Sargon.

panels.heading: The real Sargon: ancient-head payoff
panels.description: Bronze-colored ancient bearded head with damaged eyes replaces the two modern faces as narration says the real guy.
panels.camera: Cut between static inserts; underlying viewport changes.
panels.action: Artifact is a static image.
panels.visualGag: With Paul Joseph Watson and Carl Benjamin waved away, the ancient head stands for the historical Sargon. This is “the real guy,” the punchline rather than a third wrong answer.
panels.notes: The artifact’s exact museum attribution is unknown.

panels.heading: Ur-Nammu: law before prisons
panels.description: Exhibit photograph of the Ur-Nammu law tablet overlays the desktop.
panels.camera: Static historical insert.
panels.action: No character action; narration explains early punishment.

panels.heading: Hammurabi and class
panels.description: Dark inscribed stele image illustrates the next legal code.
panels.camera: Static historical insert, cut from previous illustration.
panels.action: No character action; presenter contrasts legal equality rhetoric with classes.

panels.heading: Lex talionis
panels.description: A Torah scroll illustration accompanies the ancient-law discussion.
panels.camera: Static insert over modeling.
panels.action: No character action; transition toward Greek and Roman imprisonment.

panels.heading: Rome’s holding prison
panels.description: Stone chamber and altar/red cross illustrate the Mamertine prison.
panels.camera: Static photograph.
panels.action: No character action; holding/death-row function is described.

panels.heading: Britain: bodily punishment
panels.description: A stocks photograph illustrates public corporal punishment.
panels.camera: Static photo insert, reached by a hard cut.
panels.action: No prisoner moves.
panels.visualGag: A serious punishment image sets up the monarchist pun: the next insert swaps historical royal authority for Burger King’s fake commercial king.

panels.heading: Monarchist punishment
panels.description: Burger King mascot holds two burgers, wearing a branded crown.
panels.camera: Static image overlay above the Blender interface.
panels.action: Mascot pose is frozen.
panels.visualGag: A commercial fake king literalizes the criticism of monarchist punishment.

panels.heading: Walnut Street Jail
panels.description: Historical jail engraving overlays the asset creation.
panels.camera: Static engraving insert.
panels.action: No character action; presenter explains crowded undifferentiated incarceration.

panels.heading: The expected Foucault lecture
panels.description: Black-and-white Foucault portrait appears over Blender.
panels.camera: Static portrait overlay.
panels.action: No character action; presenter refuses to pretend to have read the book.
panels.visualGag: A Foucault portrait sets up the expected Panopticon lecture, then “that’s where you’re wrong, kiddo” undercuts it. The projector turns the reversal into an old-fashioned slide lecture.

sound.text: The narrator gives “Michel Foucault” a poor French pronunciation, starting a running gag through the architecture lecture.

panels.heading: Get out the projector
panels.description: Photograph of a carousel slide projector overlays the desktop.
panels.camera: Static insert followed by cut to simulated projection.
panels.action: No projector operator is visible.
panels.visualGag: Connected audiovisual setup: a literal carousel-projector photograph and projector sound turn the spoken invitation into an old-fashioned lecture performance; the following title and slides provide the payoff.

sound.text: A slide-projector sound goes with the projector photograph.
“Foucault” gets the same poor French pronunciation again.

panels.heading: Architecture lecture begins
panels.description: Rounded illuminated slide on black reads NEOCLASSICISM, PRISONS AND THE ARCHITECTURE OF SOCIAL CONTROL.
panels.camera: Mock projection uses focus/blur and dark slide-change transitions between views.
panels.action: Static title slide; presenter directs imagined slide changes.
panels.visualGag: Illuminated slides, focus changes and slide-change sounds sustain the imaginary projector lecture.

sound.text: Projector and slide-change sounds run under the mock lecture.

panels.heading: Piranesi
panels.description: Engraved architect portrait begins the historical slide sequence.
panels.camera: Static projected slide; cuts separate slides.
panels.action: No character action; Piranesi is introduced.

panels.heading: Imaginary prisons
panels.description: Carceri engraving presents enormous stairs, vaults and complicated spatial relationships.
panels.camera: Static projected architectural engraving.
panels.action: Figures/building are drawn, not moving; narrator distinguishes fantasy from feasible prison design.

sound.text: “Louis XIV” gets a poor French pronunciation.

panels.heading: Baroque versus neoclassical
panels.description: Labeled architectural examples appear in the lecture format.
panels.camera: Static slide comparison.
panels.action: No character action; presenter distinguishes stylistic categories.

sound.text: “Beaux-Arts” is another term given a poor French pronunciation.
The full name “Claude-Nicolas Ledoux” gets a poor French pronunciation.
“Rotonde de la Villette” gets the same poor French pronunciation.
“Ledoux” again, in poor French pronunciation.
“Ferme générale” joins the terms given a poor French pronunciation.

panels.heading: Ledoux in the workshop
panels.description: Workshop screenshot introduces the available Rotonde asset.
panels.camera: Cut from historical imagery to static interface screenshot.
panels.action: Nobody downloads anything on screen; the example comes with a credit to the modder.

sound.text: “Arc-et-Senans” gets a poor French pronunciation.

panels.heading: Saltworks as surveillance
panels.description: Semicircular plan diagrams industrial buildings, housing and central supervision.
panels.camera: Static plan slide.
panels.action: No character action; narrator traces social control through the plan.
panels.visualGag: Architectural lecture context/setup: plans make social functions legible, leading through architecture parlante to the later penis-shaped brothel payoff; this plan itself is not a sexual joke.

sound.text: The shortened “Claude Ledoux” comes out in poor French pronunciation.
“Architecture parlante” gets the poor French pronunciation too.

panels.heading: Architecture parlante setup
panels.description: Visionary spherical building drawing demonstrates expressive geometric architecture.
panels.camera: Static projected drawing.
panels.action: No moving figures; buildings illustrate ideas rather than a construction sequence.
panels.visualGag: Setup: a building can announce its function through its shape.

sound.text: Another poor French pronunciation, this time of “Ledoux.”
“Chaux” gets a poor French pronunciation, and the narrator then spells the name out letter by letter.
“Ledoux” again, with the same poor French pronunciation.

panels.heading: State brothel payoff
panels.description: Brothel plan has a long central shaft, oval end and paired round chambers at its base.
panels.camera: Static plan in rounded projection aperture.
panels.action: No character action.
panels.visualGag: Penis-shaped plan makes architecture parlante a visual sexual punchline.

sound.text: “Architecture parlante” comes back in poor French pronunciation while the brothel plan is on screen.
The full name “Étienne-Louis Boullée” gets a poor French pronunciation.

panels.heading: Boullée’s library
panels.description: Grand vaulted library drawing replaces the brothel plan.
panels.camera: Cut between static architectural drawings.
panels.action: No moving people; presenter questions the open-roof construction.

sound.text: The shortened “Boullée” gets the same poor French pronunciation.

panels.heading: The sublime
panels.description: Huge severe monumental facade accompanies the scale/sublime discussion.
panels.camera: Static projected architectural drawing.
panels.action: The static drawing sets up the scale joke; the comic overlay arrives in the next panel.
panels.visualGag: The monumental facade, described as a cemetery entrance, sets up the fake PS4 Big Chungus cover in the following image.

sound.text: Another poor French pronunciation of “Boullée.”

panels.heading: Big Chungus: fake PS4 cover payoff
panels.description: A bright blue PS4-style game box labeled BIG CHUNGUS, showing an inflated Bugs Bunny/Looney Tunes figure, is pasted over the center of the monochrome Egyptian-style monumental-facade architecture slide inside the rounded projector vignette.
panels.camera: Static architectural slide with a centered game-cover insert.
panels.action: The facade stays put behind the pasted meme cover, and Bugs Bunny is a still illustration.
panels.visualGag: The scale lecture pays off here. Once the oversized monument has been called a big chungus, a fake PS4 BIG CHUNGUS game cover lands on the slide, putting an inflated Bugs Bunny meme in the middle of a high-minded projector lecture on architecture. The cover is a fake, not a real PS4 release.
panels.notes: The cover uses the Big Chungus meme of an inflated Bugs Bunny; the cartoon episode, its year and the image’s creator are unknown.

panels.heading: Newton’s immense cenotaph
panels.description: Giant spherical monument drawing dominates the slide.
panels.camera: Static projected drawing.
panels.action: No character action; enormous scale illustrates visionary ambition.
panels.visualGag: Right after the Big Chungus cover, Newton’s giant cenotaph sphere keeps the oversized-monument joke going, though the slide itself is back to plain historical architecture.

sound.text: “Ledoux” returns with its poor French pronunciation.
“Ferme générale” returns, again with a poor French pronunciation.
One more poor French pronunciation of “Boullée.”

panels.heading: Ideas travel to Russia
panels.description: Photograph of Ostankino Palace follows the French-revolution discussion.
panels.camera: Static photograph slide.
panels.action: No visible character action; presenter discusses wooden construction resembling stone.

panels.heading: The Panopticon
panels.description: Circular prison plan and section explain central observation.
panels.camera: Static architectural diagram.
panels.action: No guards/prisoners acting; narrator explains uncertainty of surveillance.

sound.text: A last poor French pronunciation of “Ledoux” comes during the Panopticon explanation.

panels.heading: Pugin: Gothic alternative
panels.description: Architect portrait introduces the counter-position to neoclassicism.
panels.camera: Static portrait slide.
panels.action: No character action; presenter frames Gothic as Christian alternative.

panels.heading: Westminster and the bell
panels.description: Photograph of the Westminster clock tower illustrates Pugin’s work.
panels.camera: Static photograph; cut from Westminster imagery.
panels.action: No character action; Big Ben correction is spoken.

panels.heading: Contrasts: new bad, old good
panels.description: Comparative plate pairs circular modern workhouse above monastic provision.
panels.camera: Static projected comparative drawing.
panels.action: Drawn figures do not act; narrator interprets the polemic.
panels.visualGag: Pugin’s polemical drawing backs up the comparison to modern posting. Its small marginal text is too small to read.

panels.heading: Haviland’s commission
panels.description: Portrait introduces John Haviland and his route to Philadelphia.
panels.camera: Static portrait slide.
panels.action: No character action; narration qualifies the claimed chain of influence.

panels.heading: Why a Gothic prison?
panels.description: Historical Eastern State exterior engraving displays gate and tall walls.
panels.camera: Static engraving, followed by exterior reference photographs.
panels.action: No moving figures.
panels.visualGag: The narrator calls back the penis-shaped brothel and the architecture parlante detour, but the screen stays on the prison exterior. The plan itself appeared earlier, in the state-brothel panel.

panels.heading: Intimidation outside, utility inside
panels.description: Interior architectural section replaces exterior views.
panels.camera: Static diagram slide; hard cuts between examples.
panels.action: No character action; narration turns from appearance to function.

panels.heading: The separate system
panels.description: PENNSYLVANIA SYSTEM / SEPARATE SYSTEM captions accompany resumed Blender capture.
panels.camera: Cut back from slides to desktop model capture.
panels.action: Model editing continues; captions name the institution’s regime.

panels.heading: Isolation by design
panels.description: Radial plan uses red highlights to mark cell areas.
panels.camera: Static diagram whose color overlay changes.
panels.action: Graphic highlights explain solitary cells and private yards.

panels.heading: Technology minimizes contact
panels.description: Cell toilet/heating photograph illustrates amenities and infrastructure.
panels.camera: Static photograph insert.
panels.action: No prisoner action shown; narration explains reducing guard contact.

panels.heading: Prison logic and schools
panels.description: University City High School architectural drawing follows prison plan/aerial comparisons.
panels.camera: Cuts between the static plan and aerial images.
panels.action: No character action; presenter extends the spatial comparison to schools.

panels.heading: Whole Pennsylvania setup
panels.description: Complete Pennsylvania outline is labeled PENNSYLVANIA over Blender.
panels.camera: Static map insert.
panels.action: Full state/name shown before truncation.
panels.visualGag: Sets up a literal “eastern Pennsylvania.”

panels.heading: Eastern half payoff
panels.description: Only eastern outline remains; intact remaining lettering reads VANIA with a clipped left fragment.
panels.camera: The map insert cuts from the whole state to its eastern half.
panels.action: Western half and corresponding letters disappear.
panels.visualGag: The geographic half-state becomes a half-name joke.

panels.heading: Numbered lives, work as favor
panels.description: Blender/reference imagery continues while narration describes prison numbers, restricted visits and required labor.
panels.camera: Cuts and reframing between the viewport and reference images; the hoods and prisoners described in the narration never appear.
panels.action: Asset construction continues; narration supplies human conditions.

panels.heading: Did it work?
panels.description: White DID IT WORK? caption overlays the modeler.
panels.camera: Static caption above changing viewport.
panels.action: The prisoner resistance described next is not acted out.
panels.visualGag: Question card sets up the deadpan negative answer.

panels.heading: Auburn’s competing system
panels.description: Historic tiered-cell interior photograph illustrates communal prison alternative.
panels.camera: Static photograph insert.
panels.action: Nothing is acted out; the narration describes silent communal labor and outside contractors.

panels.heading: From model to city
panels.description: Cities: Skylines replaces Blender as the prison is placed in local terrain.
panels.camera: Cut into the game; the oblique overhead view shifts.
panels.action: Placement and local landscape editing begin.

panels.heading: Farm plots outside the walls
panels.description: Rectangular agricultural parcels surround the newly placed walled prison.
panels.camera: Top-down and oblique game views reframe the site.
panels.action: Player lays out fields and adjoining streets while labor economics continue.

panels.heading: Capacity: BIG and SMALL
panels.description: Prison plan carries rough green BIG and red SMALL labels.
panels.camera: Static annotated plan overlay.
panels.action: Graphic labels distinguish taller and shorter cellblocks.
panels.visualGag: Low-tech labels puncture the scholarly tone while explaining capacity changes.

panels.heading: Prison tourism setup
panels.description: Niagara Falls photograph accompanies a comparison of visitor popularity.
panels.camera: Static insert over game capture.
panels.action: No tourist performance shown.
panels.visualGag: The tourism comparison leads to the Buscemi audio-tour recommendation and the fellow-kids meme that follows. The Niagara photograph itself is plain illustration.

panels.heading: Buscemi audio-tour payoff
panels.description: Buscemi wears red backward cap/hoodie, carries skateboard, and sports MUSIC lightning BAND shirt.
panels.camera: Static meme photograph overlay.
panels.action: Frozen pose, not an in-game character.
panels.visualGag: Naming the audio tour’s narrator summons the familiar “How do you do, fellow kids?” meme, shown here without its subtitle.

panels.heading: Modern prison work
panels.description: Agricultural-worker photograph illustrates crop picking.
panels.camera: Static insert, quickly replaced by other job illustrations.
panels.action: Photographed workers frozen; job descriptions are narrated.
panels.visualGag: The prison-labor montage opens soberly with farm work. The punchline, SpongeBob in a call-center headset, comes three images later.

panels.heading: Meatpacking
panels.description: Industrial meat-processing photograph continues the labor montage.
panels.camera: Hard cut between still images.
panels.action: A still photograph; it shows nothing of the working conditions.
panels.visualGag: Meatpacking keeps the job list serious.

panels.heading: Furniture for universities
panels.description: Iowa Loft Bed product page lists $745 and IPI Fort Madison Furniture.
panels.camera: Static webpage screenshot overlay.
panels.action: No shopping action; page illustrates the narrated furniture example.
panels.visualGag: The furniture page is the last straight item before the SpongeBob punchline.

panels.heading: Call-center cartoon punchline
panels.description: SpongeBob sits at an office desk wearing a headset with telephone and paperwork.
panels.camera: Cut from photographs/product page to static cartoon insert.
panels.action: Frozen cartoon work pose.
panels.visualGag: Serious labor list ends in a deliberately incongruous cartoon call-center worker.

panels.heading: Internal outsourcing argument
panels.description: Game detailing continues around the prison and surrounding farms.
panels.camera: Oblique overhead framing shifts between views.
panels.action: The player edits the landscape and neighborhood; no present-day prisoners are shown.
panels.visualGag: Before the commercial, “law and order” brings back the DUN-DUN sting and the every-time joke one last time, over ongoing game detailing.

sound.text: Law & Order’s DUN-DUN sting returns one last time before the commercial.

panels.heading: Commercial and current imprisonment
panels.description: Game view remains the background for the coworking/socialism-app joke and Manning appeal.
panels.camera: Changing game viewport; no commercial skit or Manning portrait on screen.
panels.action: City detailing continues; speech changes topic.

panels.heading: Supporters and bonus episodes
panels.description: Neighborhood/farm build continues beneath the Patreon/bonus episode pitch.
panels.camera: The overhead game view reframes.
panels.action: City detailing continues beneath the spoken lobster and PewDiePie jokes.
panels.notes: The lobster guy is Jordan Peterson. The Patreon rivalry pitch sarcastically invokes “post-modern cultural Marxism” and takes mock sole credit for his departure with “definitely no other factors”; it is not a factual claim that the narrator or supporters caused his exit.

panels.heading: Social sign-off
panels.description: White @donoteat1 handle overlays the city.
panels.camera: Static text overlay, followed by the Mastodon handle.
panels.action: No character action; presenter gives social links.

panels.heading: Mastodon and workshop
panels.description: White @donoteat@mastodon.social text accompanies final links.
panels.camera: Static text overlay over game.
panels.action: No character action; speech ends shortly afterward.

panels.heading: Finished prison reveal
panels.description: Interface-free cinematic presents finished stone entrance and surrounding fields.
panels.camera: Cut from the interface to the cinematic; successive shots reframe and reveal the hub and cellblocks.
panels.action: The finished prison appears without construction tools.

panels.heading: Radial architecture payoff
panels.description: Elevated view reveals central hub, radial blocks, enclosure and neighboring farms.
panels.camera: The view moves from close prison detail to an elevated overall framing.
panels.action: Buildings stationary; cinematic viewpoint changes.

panels.heading: City beyond the prison
panels.description: Rowhouse blocks with enclosed rear gardens and nearby industry occupy the aerial view.
panels.camera: Changing oblique aerial perspectives.
panels.action: No individual figures stand out; the camera surveys the city.

panels.heading: Gate and approach
panels.description: Frontal stone gate is centered at the end of a road between fields.
panels.camera: Successive views pull back to show more road, fields and houses.
panels.action: Stationary prison; viewpoint retreats.

panels.heading: Plan from above
panels.description: Near-vertical view shows the prison’s radial layout and rectangular field neighbors.
panels.camera: Cut to overhead then changing orientation/coverage between views.
panels.action: Stationary complex; cinematic changes viewpoint.

panels.heading: Infrastructure surrounding confinement
panels.description: Overhead cinematic shows river-side works and rectangular water basin amid woods.
panels.camera: Aerial framing moves from the riverfront to the basin and back toward the prison.
panels.action: The infrastructure is stationary and no people can be made out.

panels.heading: The whole city
panels.description: Wide aerial shows rail/industrial district, residential blocks and distant riverfront.
panels.camera: Successive shots widen and shift the view toward the riverfront.
panels.action: Stationary city; moving viewpoint supplies final contextual scale.

panels.heading: Patron credits
panels.description: My Patreons heading and dense white name columns appear on black.
panels.camera: Hard cut from the city to the credits; the names scroll upward.
panels.action: Text rolls; no character action.

panels.heading: Branded penny ending
panels.description: DNE / ONE PENNY coin emerges against black after the credits.
panels.camera: The graphic fades in, then drops toward the bottom edge.
panels.action: The coin graphic descends.
